name: Ibuprofen
executiveSummary: NSAID with analgesic, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory effects. First-line with paracetamol for fever and mild–moderate pain; pediatric dosing in mg/kg with a defined daily maximum.
indications:
## Indications

- Symptomatic treatment of **fever**.
- Mild to moderate pain (headache, toothache, myalgia, sore throat, dysmenorrhea).
- Musculoskeletal inflammatory conditions (including juvenile rheumatoid arthritis under a specific regimen).

## Precautions and contraindications

- Avoid in active peptic ulcer, GI bleeding, severe renal/hepatic failure, third trimester of pregnancy, and NSAID/ASA allergy (bronchospasm risk).
- Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.
- May mask signs of infection; reassess if fever/pain persist > 3 days.
- Caution in varicella (cutaneous/infectious risks described with NSAIDs).

> Dose by **current weight**. Confirm strength (mg/mL) before measuring volume.

adulto.presentation: Tablets/capsules 200–400–600 mg; oral suspension 20–40 mg/mL depending on brand.
adulto.dose: Fever/pain: 200–400 mg PO every 6–8 h. Usual short-course maximum: 1200 mg/day. Arthritis/inflammation under supervision: up to 1200–3200 mg/day in 3–4 doses per label and medical indication.
adulto.administration: PO with food if gastric intolerance. Do not chew modified-release tablets.
adulto.notes: Do not combine with other NSAIDs. Check interactions with anticoagulants, antiplatelets, lithium, methotrexate, and ACEI/ARB (renal function).

pediatrico.presentation: Oral suspension 2% (20 mg/mL) or 4% (40 mg/mL); pediatric tablets by brand.
pediatrico.dose: Fever/pain: **5–10 mg/kg/dose PO every 6–8 h** (commonly 7.5–10 mg/kg/dose). **Daily maximum: 30 mg/kg/day** (generally ≤ 3–4 doses/day). ANMAT-aligned example (40 mg/mL suspension): 5 mg/kg/dose if axillary T < 39 °C; 10 mg/kg/dose if T ≥ 39 °C; every 6–8 h, ≤ 3 doses/day on that label. Inflammatory pain/JRA: **20–40 mg/kg/day** divided every 6–8 h (max 40 mg/kg/day) under specialist care.
pediatrico.administration: PO. Prefer a calibrated oral syringe. Give with food if gastric upset. Do not use household spoons.
pediatrico.notes: Always calculate by weight. Verify bottle strength (20 vs 40 mg/mL) before measuring mL. Avoid < 3 months unless product-specific medical indication. Do not routinely combine with another NSAID.

neonatal.presentation: Not routine for neonatal fever/pain; IV PDA regimens are separate neonatology protocols.
neonatal.dose: Do not use as routine antipyretic/analgesic in neonates without explicit institutional indication.
neonatal.notes: IV ibuprofen for PDA is not the oral fever/pain regimen above.

stability:
## Stability / storage

- Suspension: store per label (usually room temperature, tightly closed; shake before use).
- Discard according to the manufacturer’s beyond-use date after opening.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Dyspepsia, nausea, abdominal pain, heartburn; less often: peptic ulcer/GI bleeding, rash, bronchospasm, fluid retention, elevated transaminases, acute kidney injury (especially with dehydration). Hypersensitivity reactions.
